provenance: mme. de mirbel sale, paris, 22 december 1849. allègre sale, paris, 16 may 1873, no. 295; mannheim, for sir richard wallace.

title: unavaible
description: walter scott (1771-1832): scottish novelist, poet and man of letters, created a baronet in 1820. he enjoyed an enormous reputation in his lifetime, not least in france. in 1826 he visited paris to gather material for his biography of napoleon (published the following year). he recorded in his journal that on 2 november mme. de mirbel begged him to allow her to draw his portrait and he sat to her on each of the following four days. she cried when they parted.
provenance: mme. de mirbel sale, paris, 22/12/1849. allègre sale, paris, 16/05/1873, no. 295; mannheim, for sir richard wallace.

title: caroline bonaparte, queen of naples, after isabey (?)
description: a work of very pedestrian quality. for an image of the sitter of far higher quality see m4.
provenance: probably acquired by richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: joachim murat, king of naples, after isabey
description: a work of pedestrian quality. for a version of much higher quality see m208.
provenance: probably acquired by richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: a visit to the boarding school
description: george morland was an english artist, primarily known for his paintings of animals and rustic subjects. this picture, however, is an interior scene and shows a mother visiting her daughter at boarding school. a schoolmistress leads the girl into a room where her mother waits expectantly. two other schoolgirls can also be seen peering shyly across the threshold. the painting articulates a widespread reaction against boarding schools, which was prevalent in the eighteenth century following rousseau’s call for greater parental involvement in the rearing of children. although the mother greets her child with open arms, she remains seated and the girl is clearly hesitant to see her. its companion picture, visit to the child at nurse, now in the fitzwilliam museum, illustrates the estrangement between the same mother and daughter when an infant. an early biographer stated that john raphael smith (1752-1812) ‘directed morland in painting this subject’ (hassell, 1806, p.153). the painting was engraved in 1789 by the artist’s brother-in-law, william ward (1766-1826).
provenance: anon. sale, christie's, 05 february 1791, no. 55; edward knight; durlacher, 05 march 1873; sir richard wallace.

title: the duke of wellington with colonel gurwood at apsley house
description: arthur wellesley (1769-1852), 1st duke of wellington is shown seated in the library of apsley house, the duke’s london residence following his victory at waterloo. standing beside wellington is his secretary colonel john gurwood, an army officer who had fought with wellington in the napoleonic campaigns. gurwood edited wellington’s despatches, published in 1834-9. gurwood pulls out a despatch describing wellington’s greatest victory, the defeat of napoleon at waterloo on 18 june 1815. wellington may be explaining that this despatch was begun at waterloo but finished in brussels. indeed, ‘waterloo’ is crossed out on the sheet that gurson holds out. the painting is also an accurate description of the interior of the library at apsley house; the furniture and bookcases shown in the picture are still there today. the device on the arm of the duke’s chair may be some sort of hearing aid. gurwood was also a friend of the 4th marquess of hertford, who acquired morton’s painting in 1859, presumably for sentimental reasons.
provenance: morton sale, christie's, 14 march 1846, no.38; powett; the 2nd baron northwick; his sale, phillips, 29 july 1859, no. 380; samuel mawson for richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford, cheltenham.

title: an odalisque
description: possibly painted in the 1850s, as suggested by ingamells. there was a ready market in early and mid-nineteenth century france for small-scale exotic scenes featuring odalisques (cf. bonington, 'odalisque in red', p734 and decamps, 'an odalisque', p666). the composition, with the beautiful girl looking into a mirror, recalls traditional representations of vanity.
provenance: acquired by richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: napoleon i
description: the demand for portraits of napoleon was so great that it could only be satisfied by many artists painting them. this is an independent work by muneret and does not derive, as was once thought, from an original by isabey.
provenance: probably acquired by richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: madame boulanger
description: the back of the mount is inscribed 'made boulanger'. nothing is known now of her.
provenance: probably acquired by richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: joseph and his brethren
description: the subject of this painting sets it apart from the other murillos in the wallace collection, both as a scene from the old testament and as a depiction of strong emotions. according to the book of genesis, joseph was the favourite son of his father jacob and much envied by his elder brothers. when he appeared to his brothers wearing a new coat of many colours given to him by his father, they resolved to kill him due to their jealousy. murillo depicts the moment when joseph’s brother reuben persuaded the others to mitigate the crime by abandoning the boy in an empty well. the genoese merchant giovanni bielato brought this painting, along with a number of other works by murillo, including the wallace collection’s the adoration of the shepherds and st thomas of villanueva, to his native city in c.1670. after his death they passed to the capuchin order in the city, from whom they were subsequently acquired in the nineteenth century by a british dealer. due to the unsettling subject, the 4th marquess of hertford was at first unsure whether to purchase the painting, writing to his agent samuel mawson ‘i only like pleasing pictures and the subject of the one in question may not be quite to my taste’. however, mawson’s enthusiasm seems to have won him over, as it was bought for 1,680 guineas in 1854.
provenance: giovanni bielato by 1674; by whom bequeathed to the capuchin convent, genoa, in 1681; from where purchased by william buchanan in 1805, through his agent in italy, james irvine; from whom bought by john cave of brentry house; his sale, christie's, 06 may 1843, no. 79; from where bought by samuel mawson on behalf of richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford for 1,680 guineas.

title: the virgin and child with saints
description: this is a preparatory sketch for a large composition, probably for the capuchin church in seville. saints justa and rufina are the female patron saints of seville. they were sisters who made fine earthenware pottery, which they refused to sell for pagan rituals. they were martyred in the year 304. in 1504, the tower of seville cathedral was saved from destruction during a thunder storm, and the saints came to be venerated as its saviours. murillo depicts the two sisters kneeling beside their pottery, holding their palms of martyrdom. pentiments (changes to the composition) show that they were originally painted holding a small model of the tower. with st francis of assisi and st john the baptist, they adore the vision of the virgin and child, surrounded by a host of heavenly angels. the foreboding darkness of the earth, associated with earthly misery and martyrdom, dissolves into the glorious white light of divinity. the painting was acquired by the 4th marquess of hertford in 1843.
provenance: el real monasterio de san lorenzo de el escorial, 1788. alexandre aguado, by 1839; his sale, paris, 27 march 1843, no. 39; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford, paris, 1843.

title: the marriage of the virgin
description: the subject of this painting has no biblical source but is found in the golden legend, a hagiography of saints, and in the apocryphal new testament. when mary was to be married, suitors were called to the temple, and joseph was chosen to be her husband by a sign from god. murillo depicts the moment when the virgin takes joseph's hand, as their marriage is blessed by zacharias, the high priest of the temple of jerusalem. the holy spirit in the form of a dove descends on the couple, as joseph’s rod symbolically bursts into flower, as ordained by god. murillo included a group of unsuccessful suitors to the right, one of whom breaks his rod in anger. this painting stands out for its brilliant colour range, including pairings of warm and cool colours. widely acknowledged as one of murillo’s masterpieces, it was recorded in the spanish royal collection at madrid's royal palace in 1772. it is painted on mahogany, a tropical hardwood native to central and south america and a very precious material in seventeenth-century europe.the 4th marquess of hertford bought the painting in 1848 at the laneuville sale in paris for 25,000 francs.
provenance: palacio real, madrid, 1772; joseph bonaparte, king of spain; duc de bellune; his sale, paris, 27 may 1841; reiset; laneuville; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford, london, 05 october 1848.

title: the adoration of the shepherds
description: mary reveals the newborn christ to the shepherds allowing them to be the first to recognise the son of god. they come bearing doves, the traditional offering for purification after birth, and a bound lamb. the latter symbolises christ’s later sacrifice, which the child already contemplates in the heavenly vision of a cross seen at the top of the painting. realistic details, such as the still life of the cushion, the straw hat and the dirty foot of the shepherd in the foreground, lend the picture a feeling of immediacy and intimacy that makes its message all the more convincing.the genoese merchant giovanni bielato brought this painting, along with a number of other works by murillo including the wallace collection’s joseph and his brethren and st thomas of villanueva, to his native city in c.1670. after his death they passed to the capuchin order in the city, from whom they were subsequently acquired in the nineteenth century by a british dealer.this painting was purchased by the 4th marquess of hertford in 1846.
provenance: with giovanni bielato by 1674; by whom bequeathed to the capuchin convent, genoa, in 1681; from where bought by james irvine for william buchanan in 1805; from whom bought by arthur champernowne for £800; his sale, christie's, 30 june 1820, no. 81; from where bought by piazzetta for 410 guineas; féréol-bonnemaison; his sale, paris, 17-21 april 1827, no. 42; from where bought by j.-f. boursault for 20,800 francs; his sale, paris, 07 may 1832; from where bought by edmund higginson; his sale, christie's, 06 june 1846, no. 228; from where bought by theobald for richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford for 2,875 guineas.

title: the holy family with the infant baptist
description: the subject of this painting of the holy family derives from the franciscan meditations on the life of christ. at the centre, the infant christ shows his mother a scroll referring to himself as ‘the lamb of god’ (‘ecce agn[us dei]’). lambs were symbols of innocence and humility, attributes traditionally associated with christ himself and st john the baptist. they were also sacrificial animals, thus the presence of the lamb in this painting foretells the passion of christ and the martyrdom of his cousin st john the baptist. the infant john’s cruciform staff reinforces the pathos of the message.dateable to c.1670, the painting hung in the sacristy of the capilla de la antigua in the cathedral of seville. despite efforts to conceal the painting, it was removed by marshal general soult, commander-in-chief of the french troops in spain, who had taken the city of seville in 1810. it was later owned by w. williams hope at whose sale in 1849 it was bought by the 4th marquess of hertford.
provenance: capilla de la antigua, seville cathedral; marshal soult, c. 1810. w. williams hope; his sale, christie's, 16 june 1849, no. 125; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: the annunciation
description: the painting depicts the moment described in saint luke's gospel (i, 26-38) when the angel gabriel tells mary she is to bear jesus, the son of god. murillo typically transforms the domestic scene into one of celestial glory by means of his translucent colour and vaporous painterly effects. divine golden light illuminates the kneeling mary while flying angels swirl above her. accross from mary, the angel gabriel gestures to the descending dove of the holy spirit. mary’s earthly preoccupations, symbolised by the sewing basket in the foreground, are forgotten in this moment of divine revelation. painted c.1665–70, the picture closely resembles another annunciation painted c.1688 for the capuchin church in seville.
provenance: f.-m.-g. rayneval; his sale, paris, 16 april 1838, no. 1. alexandre aguado, by 1839; his sale, paris, 27 march 1843, no 37; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: the charity of saint thomas of villanueva
description: st thomas of villanueva (1488 – 1555), an augustinian friar who became archbishop of valencia in 1544, was canonized in 1658, during the spanish counter reformation. he was famous for his charitable works and is shown here giving alms to the poor. murillo painted at least five other scenes from the saint’s life. the present picture is remarkable for the way in which the artist combines a monumental religious composition with an exceptional degree of naturalism. in accordance with the teachings of the counter reformation, the pitiful gesture of the semi-naked beggar is meant to arouse compassion in the beholder of the painting. in turn, saint thomas’s act of charity is similarly calculated to inspire admiration and emulation in the viewer.the genoese merchant giovanni bielato brought this painting, along with a number of other works by murillo including the wallace collection’s joseph and his brethren and the adoration of the shepherds, to his native city in c.1670. after his death they passed to the capuchin order in the city, from whom they were subsequently acquired in the nineteenth century by a british dealer.this painting was purchased by the 4th marquess of hertford in 1848.
provenance: with giovanni bielato by 1674; by whom bequeathed to the capuchin convent, genoa, 1681; from where bought by james irvine on behalf of william buchanan in 1805; from whom bought by william wells before 1823 for £1,000; his sale, christie's, 12 may 1848, no. 125; from where bought by richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford for 2,850 guineas.

title: the virgin and child
description: the young and beautiful virgin is depicted seated, holding the christ child on her knee. their embrace emphasises the intimate emotional bond between mother and child and thus their humanity. they do not look at each other but rather at the viewer, inspiring compassion and devotion. the virgin’s gaze is at once tender and sad, revealing her awareness of her son’s future passion. the christ child, naked but partially covered by a piece of fabric held by his mother, emanates light. his animated expression and dynamic pose bring movement which is counterbalanced by his mother’s stillness to create a sense of decorous serenity required of the subject. the figures are depicted at half-length against a neutral background of warm grey. the fictive oval frame around them creates the effect of ‘a painting within a painting’. such a compositional device was occasionally used in sevillian portraiture from the mid-seventeenth century, for example, murillo’s own self portrait at the national gallery.  it had also been used by the flemish painter rubens to frame devotional icons of the madonna and child, usually adorned with elaborate garlands of flowers. it was bought in 1849 by the 4th marquess of hertford.
provenance: w. williams hope; his sale, christie's, 16 june 1849, no. 102; mawson, for richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: the virgin and child
description: the virgin and child are shown at full length, seated on a stone seat against a dark background. it is a full-sized copy, probably from the seventeenth century, of the virgin of the rosary painted by murillo in c. 1650-1657, which was aquired by charles iv of spain before 1788 and is now in the prado museum. like another version of this composition at the palazzo pitti in florence, the wallace collection version does not include a rosary.
provenance: the condes de altamira. col. h.d. baillie, before 1823; his sale, christie's, 15 may 1858, no. 37; burgess, for richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: the virgin and child with saint rose of viterbo
description: saint rose of viterbo, identifiable from the flowers in her hand, was a thirteenth-century franciscan saint. the present work is a simplified copy after a lost original by murillo, the composition of which is known from a drawing in the biblioteca reale, turin (also a copy). the drawing shows the same figures full-length with additional saints and angels and a distant view of a preacher in a town. this composition also relates to another version of this subject by murillo with full-length figures at the museo thyssen-bornemisza (madrid) dated to c. 1670.
provenance: richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford, probably after 1856 and before 1859.

title: the virgin and child with a rosary
description: murillo treated the subject of the virgin of the rosary on several occasions, the earliest being a work painted c.1649-50 (castres, museo goya), which may be linked to murillo’s association from 1644 with the confraternity of the virgin of the rosary. in this version the christ child stands on the virgin’s knee holding a rosary, as an aid to devotion. the tenderness between mother and child is expressed in the inclination of their heads towards one another, as both look out to meet our gaze. although its attribution to murillo was questioned in the past, but the composition and brushwork are of a high enough quality to be by murillo himself.it was aquired by the 4th marquess of hertford at an unknown date.
provenance: palacio real, madrid; possibly louis, marquis de montcalm; his sale, christie's, 04 may 1849, no. 83; fuller. 4th marquess of hertford.

title: the rest on the flight into egypt
description: mary suckles the infant jesus as joseph looks on. the rocky outdoor setting suggests that the scene is intended to illustrate the story of the flight into egypt, told in saint matthew’s gospel (ii, 13-15). following a dream warning him of king herod’s search for jesus, joseph led his young family into exile in egypt.  the picture is comparable to naldini’s works of the late 1560s and 1570s. comparable works include naldini’s the holy family (florence, accademia), and the madonna and child with saints andrew and sebastian (granaiolo, castelfiorentino, san matteo).
provenance: the vicomte both de tauzia; sir richard wallace, 1872.

title: the comtesse de tillières
description: the sitter, identified by a label on the reverse, is michelle-julie-françoise-d’esparbès de lussard d’aubetterre de jonzac (c.1715-57), who married the marquis de tillières in 1730, and bore him two sons. she is shown wearing a simple powdered coiffure and a blue silk pelisse trimmed with squirrel fur. works of this kind displayed a new conception in french portraiture that aimed above all at ‘naturalness’, which was to find its most notable expression in the work of the pastellist maurice quentin de la tour.nattier painted this portrait at the time of his greatest success, after his portrait of the french queen maria leczinska of 1748 (see p437). the late 1740s mark a moment in his career when he was increasingly concentrating on the sitter's personality.
provenance: acquired by richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: mademoiselle de clermont en sultane
description: little is known of this group portrait showing a seated white female figure, currently identified as marie-anne de bourbon (1697–1741), better known as mademoiselle de clermont, and several unidentified black models.the painting aligns with the genre of historicised portraits, that is, representations of actual sitters in a fantasy or allegorical setting. the seated woman at the centre was the youngest child of louis iii de bourbon, prince de condé and of mademoiselle de nantes, an illegitimate (though subsequently recognised) daughter of louis xiv.nattier shows mademoiselle de clermont in the guise of a sultana in a harem, an erotically charged space in the western imagination. the painting is thus an early example of 'turquerie' — a depiction in an imaginary 'turkish' vein — that slowly emerged as a new fashion in the years around 1720. this setting provided the artist with an excuse to include clermont’s exposed lower legs and knees, elements that would have been unacceptable in a formal court portrait.the fantasy setting may also provide some rationale for the presence of the other women in this painting: six black figures who are grouped around the seated clermont. as people of colour, such women would not have been typical habitués of the eighteenth-century french court; their presence here thus enhances the exotic mood created by the ‘turkish’ allusions. today, their identities are unknown, though given the specificity with which the artist has rendered their features, we might suppose he worked from actual models or print representations, rather than purely from his imagination. it is also worth noting that the painting was made only a few short decades after the establishment, by clermont’s ancestor louis xiv, of the code noir. this notorious document codified slavery in the french colonial empire. it is likely, therefore, that the women represented here would have been understood by contemporary viewers as enslaved. alluding to power dynamics that make the today’s viewer uncomfortable, the presence of these women of colour in relation to clermont would have reinforced the eighteenth-century viewer’s perception of her wealth and status.the fact that the image is so dominated by clermont may suggest that she was deeply involved in constructing its iconography. yet nattier’s painting contrasts markedly with clermont’s public image and her official function of surintendante de la maison de la reine (senior lady-in-waiting to the queen) from 1725. it may have been intended for her private collection, or as a gift from her to a close associate. unfortunately, the early provenance of the work is unknown. the painting was only shown at the salon of 1742, nine years after its creation, a clear indication that its public display was not acceptable while clermont was still alive.in the context of our ongoing equity, diversity, and inclusion initiative here at the wallace collection, research on this painting, its making, and its meanings is still ongoing. if you have any information to share, we invite you to contact collection@wallacemuseum.org.
provenance: the duc de saint aignan; his sale, paris, 17 june 1776, no. 176. véron sale, paris, 17 march 1858, no. 77; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: the marquise de belestat
description: the sitter was identified by a label, as marie-charlotte de châteaurenaud, who married the marquis de belestat of toulouse (1725-1807) in 1752. she succeeded her mother as a lady-in-waiting to the daughters of louis xv and attended the court at versailles in 1754 and 1755. in 1754 she was involved in a dispute at cards with the comte de lorge, an incident which voltaire commemorated in verse. her commission to nattier is probably linked to her court career at the time. the portrait is of a type commonly used by the artist to depict young female sitters: she is dressed in the formal robe à la française with blue silk drapery, three-quarter length, without hands, in front of a neutral background. in contrast to other contemporary portraitists nattier’s aim was not to represent the psychology of his sitters but to provide a fashionable and beautiful image according to society ideals.
provenance: vicomte de gavarrat-rouaix; his sale, paris, 06-07 february 1867, no. 83; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: marie leszcynska, queen of france, after nattier
description: marie leszczynska (1703-68), daughter of stanislaus leszczynski, duke of lorraine and former king of poland, married king louis xv of france in 1725 when he was fifteen. they had ten children together. this miniature is based on a famous portrait of the queen by jean-marc nattier painted in 1748, today in the châteaux de versailles. the present artist portrayed the queen in bust rather than three-quarter length. many painted copies of nattier's iconic portrait are known, including a reduced version at the wallace collection (p437).
provenance: acquired by 1872.

title: le maréchal duc de richelieu
description: this is a contemporary reduced copy of a picture painted by jean-marc nattier in 1732 to decorate the duke’s dining room at the château de richelieu (lisbon, museu calouste gulbenkian). louis-françois-armand vignerot du plessis, duc de richelieu (1696-1788), great-nephew of cardinal richelieu, became a maréchal de france in 1748. he is shown just before his full investiture as a knight of the order of the saint-esprit, wearing the white costume of a novice, while the cloak, gloves and order of a full knight lie on the sofa beside him. the image was calculated to remind the observer that he had been called to the order of the saint esprit in 1729 at the age of only thirty-two, three years before the normal qualifying age of thirty-five.
provenance: didot sale, paris, 06 april 1825, no. 212; leroi. l.-d. vèze sale, paris, 10 december 1846, no. 96. p.-c. prosteau de montlouis; his sale, paris, 05-06 may 1851, no. 175. richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: marie leszczynska, queen of france
description: marie leszczynska (1703–1768), daughter of stanislaus leszczynski, duke of  lorraine and former king of poland, married king louis xv of france in 1725 and bore him ten children. she became known for her pious nature, which nattier brilliantly conveyed in a portrait of 1748, today in the châteaux of versailles. the wallace collection's picture is a reduced eighteenth-century copy of this famous painting. the queen had asked nattier to portray her en habit de ville (in a day dress), without the traditional regal accoutrements found in royal portraits. the resulting image, praised for its simplicity, heralded a new naturalism in french eighteenth-century portraiture. nattier's portrait was the last and most iconic image of the queen. it was engraved by jacques-nicolas tardieu in 1755. numerous painted copies were produced at the cabinet du roi in versailles, which may be where the wallace collection's painting originated.the conservation of marie leszczynska, queen of france was made possible in 2018 by the generous support of the john s cohen foundation
provenance: possibly dr. gaudinot sale, paris, 15-16 february 1869, no. 70; from where bought by the duc de mouchy; with richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford, by 1871.

title: interior of antwerp cathedral
description: this painting of c. 1648-1650 represents the interior of the cathedral of our lady in antwerp, which was only completed in this form in c. 1617, and was filled with new artwork, including altarpieces by rubens. pieter neeffs the elder (b. c. 1578) specialized in painting church interiors for the open market. he painted a number of views of the interior of antwerp cathedral, including comparable views now at the kunsthistorisches museum, vienna and in the royal museum of fine arts, brussels. each painting differs in the representation of the figures and their interactions. his skill in rendering perspective was particularly admired. here he has exaggerated the height and length of the nave to emphasise the sense of occupying this uniquely large, public, indoor space which sets the stage for a range of anecdotal details. mass is being celebrated at a guild altar on the right side of the nave, while other figures walk around the space, even with their dogs. the figures here represent a cross -section of antwerp’s hierarchical society: the aristocracy and clergy, wealthy merchants and the destitute who seek their charity. conservation treatment carried out in 2024 involved removing layers of discoloured varnish and later conservator’s retouchings. close observation of the paint surface during conservation has also revealed that the figures were painted after the architectural components were finished. it is thought that they were painted by a specialist figure painter, probably frans francken ii. only pieter neeffs signed the work; his signature can be seen on the pillar on the right foreground, as if chiseled into the stone.
provenance: acquired by francis charles seymour-conway, 3rd marquess of hertford.

title: a winter scene
description: van der neer excelled in depicting meteorological conditions. the luminous effects of sunset, dawn, moon and firelight create a sense of space and atmosphere in even his smallest landscapes. a winter scene is one of van der neer’s most accomplished evocations of wintry light, one of several scenes in which the artist depicts falling snow. flickering dabs of white paint highlight the branches of trees, lightly powder the shoulders of some of the figures and lie scattered on the rough ground.
provenance: [probably anon. sale, rotterdam, 03 april 1850, no. 46.] herman de kat; his sale, paris, 02-03 may 1866, no. 54; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: canal scene by moonlight
description: van der neer began to paint nocturnes c.1645-50, though the rather cursory handling of this work suggests a later date. the scene is constructed in van der neer’s habitual manner, with a central river reaching into the distance and the creation of perspectival recession into depth. picturesque interest is established by the fishermen hauling their nets in the foreground.
provenance: acquired by richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: a river scene: evening
description: aert van der neer established himself as a landscape painter in amsterdam in 1632. he specialised in monochrome landscapes, particularly moonlight and winter scenes. probably painted in the 1640s, the picture displays the artist’s characteristic use of blues, greys and ochres and is comparable to sunset on the ijssel in the petit palais, paris.
provenance: désiré van den schrieck; his sale, louvain, 08-11 april 1861, no. 60; wallace, for richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: a skating scene
description: in a skating scene van der neer makes use of a slightly raised vantage-point, from which he depicts a large expanse of sky. a sense of distance is created by the delicate silhouettes of trees and buildings traced against the horizon. small figures, which recall the work of hendrick avercamp, animate the foreground and middle distance and provide picturesque interest: they chat, skate, ride in sleighs and play kolf.
provenance: b. beeckman sale, rotterdam, 09 june 1828, no. 30; van den berg. [possibly m. zachery sale, christie's, 31 march 1838, no. 18; fuller, for  nieuwenhuys]. charles brind; his sale, christie's, 12 may 1849, no. 59; samuel mawson, for richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: scene on a canal
description: of weak execution, the composition is probably copied after a lost work by van der neer which is known from an engraving of 1763, and of which there are several other versions.
provenance: stevens sale, antwerp, 09 august 1837, no. 111; gruyter. a. w. c. baron van nagell van ampsen sale, the hague, 05 september 1851, no. 42; roos. anatole demidoff; his sale, paris, 13 january 1863, no. 23; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: a river scene by moonlight
description: this moonlight scene of a river bears is typical of van der neer’s compositions. the winding movement of the river draws the eye towards the horizon, past the cattle in the middle ground. however, the smooth brushwork does not seem to resonate with van der neer’s usual style, and so it may be a later copy.
provenance: paul périer; his [anon.] sale, paris, 16 march 1843, no. 29; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: a lady drawing
description: son of aert van der neer (also represented in the wallace collection), eglon studied first with his father, and later with the history painter jacob van loo. he was in france c.1654, but returned to holland, and by 1664 was living in rotterdam, where he remained until 1679. during this period, he developed his characteristic refined genre scenes, which recall the leiden ‘fine painters’ in technique and ter borch in subject matter. van der neer painted a number of pictures with elegant female figures occupied in polite occupations, such as reading and playing musical instruments. they show exemplary feminine behaviour among the leisured classes. this young woman draws from bronze statuettes based on ancient sculpture.
provenance: [possibly kamermans sale, rotterdam, 03 october 1825, no. 21; lamme]. edmund higginson, by 1841; his sale, christie's, 06 june 1846, no. 185; goldsmith. charles scarisbrick; his sale, christie's, 11 may 1861, no. 351; colman. richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: kilchurn castle
medium: watercolour with gum varnish on card.
description: kilchurn castle is at the east end of loch awe, strathclyde. looming over the castle are the grampian mountains, with ben cruachan the foremost peak.  before he turned his attention increasingly to landscape gardening nesfield had a considerable reputation as a painter of landscapes, being particularly admired for his depictions of turbulent water - ruskin referred to him as 'nesfield of the radiant cataract'.
provenance: elhanan bicknell; his sale, christie's, 29 april 1863, no. 93; wells for richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: portrait of a lady with an orange
description: the lady is seated in front of a relief decorated with swags and putti. beside her is an orange tree, and in her hand she holds one of its fruit. both tree and fruit may refer to the house of orange-nassau, although the orange tree was also generally regarded as a symbol of purity, chastity and generosity, all desirable attributes for a well-bred lady (cf. boucher p418).
provenance: acquired by richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: lady with a watch
description: in this small-scale genre scene a woman holds a watch to her ear. her right hand slips inside her jacket as if testing her heartbeat to the rhythm of the little clock. the lit candle in the back may symbolise the flame of desire, but it may also suggest that this picture is a vanitas, intended to remind the viewer of the transience of human life and love. the lady’s costume, with its elegant ermine-trimmed jacket, recalls the work of gerard ter borch.
provenance: [possibly anon. sale, amsterdam, 05 or 09 august 1739, no. 9; and probably henry artaria sale, phillips, 23 april 1850, no. 82]. francis seymour-conway, marquess of hertford.

title: a child plucking a rose
description: a child plucking a rose is almost certainly a pendant to a young lady playing the guitar (also in the wallace collection). they were painted in the same year, are of the same size and format, and share the same provenance. this painting shows a much younger girl, plucking a rose, symbolic of purity and love. she takes the flower from a pot placed on an entablature supported by putti, the naked children traditionally associated with venus, goddess of love. since the pictures were painted in the same year, are of similar size and format, and share the same provenance, it is likely that they depict members of the same family.
provenance: counts of hornes. herman de kat; his sale, paris, 02-03 may 1866, no. 58; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: a young lady playing the guitar
description: the son of a german sculptor, caspar netscher moved to arnhem and later studied under gerard ter borch in deventer. he settled in the hague, becoming a member of the painters’ society, pictura, in 1662. during this period he specialised in small-scale genre scenes (of which the lace maker, also in the wallace collection, is the finest example). a young lady playing the guitar depicts a fashionably dressed girl, seated at a table covered by a sumptuous rug. holding a guitar, she shows off her musical accomplishments.
provenance: counts of hornes. herman de kat; his sale, 02-03 and 07-08 may 1866, no. 57; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: the lace maker
description: a pupil of gerard ter borch, netscher specialised in small-scale genre scenes in the manner of his teacher. later in his career, from c.1667, he focused instead on portraits of patrician subjects. netscher’s undisputed masterpiece, the lace maker, is one of the most successful representations of idealised female virtue in dutch art. in the seventeenth century, women were frequently depicted as dangerous creatures, prone to vice if left to their own devices. contemporary moralists recommended marriage and housewifery as the only fit occupations for women. within the home, one of the housewife’s principal duties was to maintain its order and cleanliness, implied in this picture by the broom propped against the wall on the left. the girl’s modest woollen dress implies her lack of vanity, while her absorption in the delicate and difficult task of lace-making underlines her seriousness and moral rectitude. such an image of the demure housewife, prudent and chaste, had wider implications too, since the home and its correct organization were considered of supreme importance in determining the moral fate of dutch society as a whole.
provenance: [possibly jacob vallensis]. johan pompe van meerdevoort; his sale, souterwoude, 19 may 1780, no. 5; delfos, probably for p.c. van leyden; diederick van leyden; his sale, paris, 05-07 november 1804, no. 67; paillet, for francis charles seymour-conway, 3rd marquess of hertford; his sales, christie's, 04 july 1807, no. 86, bt. in, and christie's, 02 march 1808, no. 90, bt. in.

title: the gentle student
description: this painting acquired some renown after it was engraved by charles rolls in 1833 and by samuel sangster in 1847. its purchase was recommended to lord hertford by his london agent samuel mawson.
provenance: gen. the hon. edmund phipps, by 1833; the hon. edmund phipps; his sale, christie's, 25 june 1859, no. 82; samuel mawson for richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: a boy with a falcon and leash
description: little is known about van noordt. described as from amsterdam by a contemporary biographer, it is not known with whom he trained, although the works of jacob backer appear to have been a strong influence. his dated paintings range from 1653 to 1676. the boy’s rich costume lends an aura of refinement to the portrait, recalling the elegance of van dyck (q.v.) and of van noordt’s flemish contemporaries such as gonzales coques (q.v.), while his occupation suggests the privileged status of the huntsman. following the extension of hunting rights, which had been an exclusive privilege of the aristocracy, it became common for the wealthy dutch middle classes to have themselves depicted enjoying this new privilege.
provenance: sir richard wallace, c. 1872.

title: a boy with a falcon
description: owing to its similarity to another painting in the wallace collection, the boy with a hawk was thought in the nineteenth century to be by nicolaes maes. however, it reveals the characteristic broad handling of van noordt.
provenance: george keith, 10th earl marischal. a.-c.-c.-b. perregaux, comte de perregaux; his sale, paris, 08-09 december 1841, no. 17; duchâtel. richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford, before 1848.

title: river scene
description: according to the catalogue of a sale in 1850 which included this painting, amsterdam is represented in the misty distance. the composition recalls seventeenth-century dutch paintings, but also the river scenes popularised in the 1820s by bonington and his contemporaries (cf. bonington, 'on the seine near mantes', p339). the wallace collection's picture was painted in the year before nuyen's early death at the age of twenty six.
provenance: william ii of holland; his sale, the hague, 15 august 1850, no. 83; weenink, for baron van brienan van groote lindt; groote lindt sale, paris, 03 may 1870, no. 54; leroy, for richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: sir richard leveson
medium: watercolour and bodycolour vellum laid on plain card
description: isaac oliver was the son of huguenot parents from rouen. his father, the goldsmith pierre olivier, had settled in england with his family by 1568. isaac learned miniature painting with nicholas hilliard, a choice which reflected the close ties between goldsmiths and miniature painters at the time. hilliard and oliver became the two eminent miniature painters of the period. oliver’s career was in the ascendant throughout and he became official miniature painter to queen anne of denmark in 1605, and a member of the household of henry frederick, prince of wales, of whom he painted several brilliant portraits.this miniature is typical of oliver’s style. the sitter, sir richard leveson (c.1570–1605), a naval officer during the anglo-spanish war (1585–1604), was knighted for his successes during the cadiz expedition in 1596 and played an important role in 1601 fending off the spanish attempts to land in ireland. in 1604 leveson was appointed vice-admiral of england by james i but died the following year. around the time that oliver painted the portrait, leveson’s private life had changed dramatically. after his wife had become insane in 1602, he took up with a new partner, mary fitton, with whom he had a child in 1603.oliver’s portrait of sir richard leveson exists in three versions, all of which seem to be autograph. the prime example, in a private collection, is identical in size to the version in the wallace collection but differs in some details, in particular in the rendering of leveson’s dress.
provenance: acquired by 1904.

title: interior with peasants
description: van ostade studied with frans hals in his native haarlem. his fellow student, the flemish painter adriaen brouwer, would also have a profound impact on him, both in terms of style and low-life subject matter. throughout his career he also provided figures for other artists, including jacob van ruisdael and pieter saenraedam. he was the most important dutch draughtsman and etcher of genre subjects of his day, and his pupils included his brother isaack and jan steen. in interior with peasants, the mother attempting to feed her child probably recalls the seventeenth-century dutch proverb ‘open wide when someone offers you pap, or else later you will receive nothing.’ ostade was a sensitive observer of mother and child relationships, and appears to have been the first contemporary artist to explore this theme, common in dutch genre painting.
provenance: ange-laurent de lalive de jully, by 1757; his sale, paris, 02-14 may 1770, no. 13; donjeu. dutartre; his sale, paris, 19 march 1804, no. 26; delastre [or descartes]. francis charles seymour-conway, 3rd marquess of hertford, by 1829.

title: buying fish
description: throughout his career ostade painted and etched scenes of people earning their living. scenes of markets, in keeping with the commercial values of the northern netherlands, were also favoured by dutch artists and collectors in the seventeenth century onwards. ostade painted a number of such subjects in the 1660s and 1670s, and the present picture has the broader handling, brighter palette and larger figures of his later works.
provenance: daniel wade acraman, 1829. michael zachary; his sale, christie's, 30-31 march 1838, no. 44; fuller, for nieuwenhuys. paul périer; his [anon.] sale, paris, 17 march 1843, no. 30; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: boors carousing
description: this is a copy by an unknown painter after a signed and dated painting by ostade of 1660 in the dresden gemäldegalerie. the figures are set deep within the kind of spacious and gloomy tavern often depicted by ostade.
provenance: the 1st earl granville; his sale, christie's, 21 june 1845, no. 16; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: a market place
description: the brother of adriaen van ostade, isack van ostade specialised in landscapes and outdoor genre scenes. this painting shows the prinzipalmarkt in münster, germany, looking towards the church of saint lamberti at the time of the peace congress of westphalia (1645-8). ostade is not known to have travelled to münster himself, and possibly was indebted for his composition to studies by ter borch, who had been there accompanying the dutch delegation to the peace negotiations.
provenance: paul périer; his [anon.] sale, paris, 17 march 1843, no. 32; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: a winter scene
description: this painting is typical of the atmospheric, silvery-grey winter scenes produced by van ostade, in which he successfully marries anecdotal detail, with a convincing evocation of the winter landscape. figures of all ages and from different social classes play and go about their business on the ice. this picture was given to lady wallace by alfred de rothschild in exchange for another painting by isack van ostade, and thus was the last work of art to enter the wallace collection before lady wallace’s bequest in 1897.
provenance: william cririe, by 1842; his sale, christie's, 3 june 1871, no. 36; bought by agnew for 285 gn.; r. kirkman hodgson; alfred de rothschild, after 1884; from whom given to lady wallace between 1890 and 1898.

title: a village scene
description: a copy of a smaller picture by isack van ostade, dated 1645, in the national gallery of art, washington.
provenance: acquired by francis charles seymour-conway, 3rd marquess of hertford, by 1842.

title: hawk attacking a wild duck
description: a vertical varient of a horizontal composition by oudry, prepared in 1737, the main version in schwerin (staatliches museum schwerin/ludwigslust/güstrow, inv. no. g219). watercolours of the hawk and of the ducks are attributed to jacques-charles oudry (oudry album; cambridge, massachusetts, fogg art museum). this picture is one of a so-called ‘set’ of three attributed to oudry sold at the baron de commailles sale in 1855. a further picture from the same group is in the wallace collection and is now attributed to nicolas desportes (p623). the painting has long been regarded as a work by jean-baptiste oudry or his workshop, the attribution to his son was suggested by pierre jacky.
provenance: the baron de commailles; his sale, paris, 2 august 1855, no. 40. richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: dog pointing pheasants
description: the painting was one of a set of four overdoors (with p627, p629 and p631) commissioned by the intendant des finances and director of the département des ponts et chaussées, daniel-charles trudaine for his château at montigny-lencoup, near melun, which later became a hunting lodge for louis xv (cf. boucher p482 and p489). p627 was painted in 1747, the other three paintings of the set in the following year. their uneven quality, reflecting their position as overdoors, suggests that oudry’s workshop including his son jacques-charles may have helped with their execution, although preparatory drawings confirm that the designs were by his father. jean-baptiste considered them important works as he chose to exhibit them at the 1748 salon.
provenance: daniel-charles trudaine; george de stacpoole, 1818; richard stacpoole; his sale, paris, 01-3 march 1852, no. 6. richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: the dead wolf
description: together with its pendant (p630), the painting is one of the early masterpieces by oudry, one of the most brilliant still-lifes of the eighteenth century and one of the earliest major works of a new style, the rococo. both works are likely to have been inserted into the wood panelling of a room used for dining, probably of a country house. their size and the emphasis on the aristocratic privilege of the hunt indicate an important patron and first owner who is unfortunately unknown. several copies after both works suggest that they might have been in a more prominent location. the most important copies are in the château of condé-en-brie, once owned by the leriget de la faye. he belonged to a circle of major collectors in paris around the comtesse de verrue and jean de jullienne to which the first owner might have been associated. oudry rendered the two scenes in a free, loose brushwork in pastel-like colours. both elements reflect a recent vogue for contemporary venetian painting among french painters around 1720. the objects are arranged close to the picture surface without much spatial depth in the arrangement. instead, they create a asymmetrical, pattern organised along curves and swirls, a principle that will become typical for the nascent rococo style. this richness of colours and surface patterns is characteristic of the so-called genre pittoresque, the new french decorative style of the 1720s.oudry had become a member of the paris academy as a history painter in 1719, an ambition which might be related to the strong narrative elements in both paintings.
provenance: marquis d'arbaud-jouques; his sale, paris, 26 february 1858, no. 18; lebeuf de montgermont; mme. lebeuf, 1860. by 1871, richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: hawk attacking partridges and a rabbit
description: the painting was one of a set of four overdoors (with p625, p629 and p631) commissioned by the intendant des finances and director of the département des ponts et chaussées, daniel-charles trudaine for his château at montigny-lencoup, near melun, which later became a hunting lodge for louis xv (cf. boucher p482 and p489). it was painted in 1747, the other three paintings of the set in the following year. their uneven quality, reflecting their position as overdoors, suggests that oudry’s workshop including his son jacques-charles may have helped with their execution, although preparatory drawings confirm that the designs were by his father. jean-baptiste considered them important works as he chose to exhibit them at the 1748 salon. a preparatory drawing for the composition is preserved at the philadelphia museum of art, detail studies are in the staatliches museum in schwerin and untraced.
provenance: daniel-charles trudaine; george de stacpoole, 1818; richard stacpoole; his sale, paris, 1-3 march 1852, no. 6. richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: fox in the poultry yard
description: the painting was one of a set of four overdoors (with p625, p627 and p631) commissioned by the intendant des finances and director of the département des ponts et chaussées, daniel-charles trudaine for his château at montigny-lencoup, near melun, which later became a hunting lodge for louis xv (cf. boucher p482 and p489). p627 was painted in 1747, the other three paintings of the set in the following year. their uneven quality, reflecting their position as overdoors, suggests that oudry’s workshop including his son jacques-charles may have helped with their execution, although preparatory drawings confirm that the designs were by his father. jean-baptiste considered them important works as he chose to exhibit them at the 1748 salon. an early study of 1746 for the painting is in the kupferstichkabinett, staatliche museen zu berlin, a compositional drawing of 1748 in a private collection.
provenance: daniel-charles trudaine; george de stacpoole, 1818; richard stacpoole; his sale, paris, 1-3 march 1852, no. 6. richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

description: together with its pendant (p626), the painting is one of the early masterpieces by oudry, one of the most brilliant still-lifes of the eighteenth century and one of the earliest major works of a new style, the rococo. both works are likely to have been inserted into the wood panelling of a room used for dining, probably of a country house. their size and the emphasis on the aristocratic privilege of the hunt indicate an important patron and first owner who is unfortunately unknown. several copies after both works suggest that they might have been in a more prominent location. the most important copies are in the château of condé-en-brie, once owned by the leriget de la faye. he belonged to a circle of major collectors in paris around the comtesse de verrue and jean de jullienne to which the first owner might have been associated. oudry rendered the two scenes in a free, loose brushwork in pastel-like colours. both elements reflect a recent vogue for contemporary venetian painting among french painters around 1720. the objects are arranged close to the picture surface without much spatial depth in the arrangement. instead, they create a asymmetrical, pattern organised along curves and swirls, a principle that will become typical for the nascent rococo style. this richness of colours and surface patterns is characteristic of the so-called genre pittoresque, the new french decorative style of the 1720s.oudry had become a member of the paris academy as a history painter in 1719, an ambition which might be related to the strong narrative elements in both paintings.
provenance: marquis d'arbaud-jouques; his sale, paris, 26 february 1858, no. 17; lebeuf de montgermont; mme. lebeuf, 1860. by 1871, richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: spaniel pursuing ducks
description: the painting was one of a set of four overdoors (with p625, p627 and p629) commissioned by the intendant des finances and director of the département des ponts et chaussées, daniel-charles trudaine for his château at montigny-lencoup, near melun, which later became a hunting lodge for louis xv (cf. boucher p482 and p489). p627 was painted in 1747, the other three paintings of the set in the following year. their uneven quality, reflecting their position as overdoors, suggests that oudry’s workshop including his son jacques-charles may have helped with their execution, although preparatory drawings confirm that the designs were by his father. jean-baptiste considered them important works as he chose to exhibit them at the 1748 salon. a compositional drawing for the painting is in a private collection.
provenance: daniel-charles trudaine; george de stacpoole, 1818; richard stacpoole; his sale, paris, 1-3 march 1852, no. 6. richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: an italian peasant girl
description: perhaps painted during papety’s stay at the french academy in rome 1836-41. although more sentimental than most, it is characteristic of the studies of italian popular types painted by many northern artists in italy (cf. winterhalter, a girl of ariccia', p669).
provenance: acquired by richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: a french peasant girl
description: a french counterpart of the italian peasant girl in papety, 'an italian peasant girl', p567. both pictures recall contemporary costume books.
provenance: thévenin sale, paris, 27 january 1851, no. 56; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: the temptation of saint hilarion
description: exhibited at the paris salon of 1844. saint hilarion (c.291-371) was a hermit who founded many monasteries in palestine. he was a follower of saint anthony abbot (see delaroche, the temptation of saint anthony', p311), and like him endured many temptations by satan. sexual temptation is the theme of several paintings by papety. an icon visible in the cave demonstrates his unusual interest in art of byzantine origin, even before he visited greece for the first time in 1846.
provenance: van isacker?. richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford, by 1860.

title: a neapolitan fisherman
description: although the painting bears a false signature of léopold robert, papety’s original signature underneath was revealed by local cleaning in 1985. curiously the false signature seems to have been added between 1875 and 1890, when the painting was owned by sir ricahrd wallace. papety was one of many artists influenced by léopold robert’s scenes from italian popular life which were much admired in the nineteenth century (cf. léopold robert p590-2). he visited naples in 1839.
provenance: probably papety sale, paris, 15-6 january 1850, no. 25. adolphe moreau.

title: an italian peasant woman and child
medium: watercolour and bodycolour wit gum varnish on paper
description: perhaps painted during papety’s stay at the french academy in rome 1836-41 (cf. papety, 'an italian peasant girl', p567). paintings of peasants - often seen as handsome, natural and romantic figures - were often produced by northern artists visiting italy in the nineteenth century.
provenance: acquired by richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: a chinese girl
medium: watercolour and bodycolour with gum varnish on paper
description: the inscription on the wall - written by someone unfamiliar with the chinese language - may be translated ‘the virtuous woman does not have several husbands’. the watercolour is an early example of the fascination with the far east which was to be a feature of nineteenth-century painting.
provenance: acquired by richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: fête galante with a dancing couple
description: the elegant city dwellers on the right are accompanied by village musicians. the setting is italianate, referring to sixteenth-century pastorals (scenes of ideal, southern country life). pater painted the work in the late 1720s, when his style became more independent from watteau's and his palette became much lighter. the embracing couple in the right mid-distance were revealed during cleaning in 1965-6, and had probably been painted out for reasons of modesty in the early nineteenth century. a very similar composition by pater was sold in new york (sotheby's, 29 may 2003, lot 61).
provenance: charles meigh; his sale, christie's, 09 june 1855, no. 53; caw, for richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: le concert amoureux (the amourous concert)
description: the painting is a beautiful example of the fête galante, and can be dated on stylistic grounds to c. 1730/1733.  it comes from a set of four (with p386, p397 and p400) that includes two musical scenes and two depictions of games that were probably meant as pairs of pendants. versions of the two musical scenes exist in schloss sanssouci in potsdam, one of them of "le concert amoureux" with only minute variations. vertical scenes are relatively rare in pater's work, and one can assume that this choice was related to the series of four that might have been painted for a specific context. the set was engraved by pierre fillœul, 1739, and a sentimental poem by charles moraine interpreting the amorous subject matter of the picture accompanied each print. the background landscape evokes an ideal rustic setting combining french and italian elements.
provenance: nicolas-alexandre de ségur, 1737/1739-1755. richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: la conversation intéressante (the interesting conversation)
description: the painting is a beautiful example of the fête galante, and can be dated on stylistic grounds to c. 1730/1733.  it comes from a set of four (with p383, p397 and p400) that includes two musical scenes and two depictions of games that were probably meant as pairs of pendants. versions of only the two musical scenes exist in schloss sanssouci in potsdam. vertical scenes are relatively rare in pater's work, and one can assume that this choice was related to the series of four that might have been painted for a specific context. the set was engraved by pierre fillœul 1739, each print accompanied by a sentimental poem by charles moraine interpreting the amorous subject matter of the picture. the verses which accompany la conversation intéressante draw a contrast between the lady inclined to love seated on the ground and the ambivalent attitude of the lady on the swing. moraine's poem does not necessarily reflect pater's original intention but can help to understand the perception of the scene in the eighteenth century. in the eighteenth century swing was seen as a symbol of the changing nature of love, in particular of women.
provenance: nicolas-alexandre de ségur, 1737/1739-1755. richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: la danse (the dance)
description: the painting is a beautiful example of the fête galante, and can be dated on stylistic grounds to c. 1730/1733.  it comes from a set of four (with p383, p386 and p400) that includes two musical scenes and two depictions of games that were probably meant as pairs of pendants. versions of the two musical scenes, including "la danse", exist in schloss sanssouci in potsdam. the potsdam painting shows a different bagpipe player on the right. vertical scenes are relatively rare in pater's work, and one can assume that this choice was related to the series of four that might have been painted for a specific context. the set was engraved by pierre fillœul 1739, each print accompanied by a sentimental poem by charles moraine interpreting the amorous subject matter of the picture. the background landscape evokes an ideal rustic setting combining french and italian elements.
provenance: nicolas-alexandre de ségur, 1737/1739-1755. richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: le colin-maillard (blind man's buff)
description: the painting is a beautiful example of the fête galante, and can be dated on stylistic grounds to c. 1730/1733.  it comes from a set of four (with p383, p386 and p397) that includes two musical scenes and two depictions of games that were probably meant as pairs of pendants. versions of only the two musical scenes exist in schloss sanssouci in potsdam. vertical scenes are relatively rare in pater's work, and one can assume that this choice was related to the series of four that might have been painted for a specific context. the set was engraved by pierre fillœul 1739, each print accompanied by a sentimental poem by charles moraine interpreting the amorous subject matter of the picture. the background landscape evokes an ideal rustic setting combining french and italian elements.
provenance: nicolas-alexandre de ségur, 1737/1739-1755. richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: the boudoir
description: the subject probably illustrates one of lafontaine's "contes". eight scenes by pater after lafontaine were engraved by pierre fillœul; the engravings were announced between 1733 and 1736. the painting in the wallace collection was not engraved, so that the identification of the scene is uncertain. fillœul owned ten paintings by pater and this might have been one of the two additional ones that were not engraved. they were most likely all painted as model for the engraver. a smaller painting (panel, 16,5 x 20,3 cm) is in the david-weill collection in paris. it is sketchier in style and might have been a first step towards the more finished larger version in the wallace collection. a drawing for the reclining woman is in the musée jacquemart-andré in paris. the paintings after lafontaine and a series of fourteen paintings after paul scarron in potsdam are pater's masterworks as an illustrator.
provenance: johann anton de peters; his sale, paris, 09 march 1779, no. 96. anon. sale, paris, 09 june 1868, no. 1; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: fête galante by a fountain
description: the work is a typical fête galante in the immediate tradition of watteau. the composition follows works by watteau from the late 1710s such as the "rendez-vous de chasse" (p416) at the wallace collection, a painting that inspired a work by pater in the dulwich picture gallery. the figures on the fountain that seem strangely alive directly follow watteau. the figures and their groupings are typical for the fête galante as established by watteau but they show pater's own very personal style. the dark landscape, strong local colours, the reddish tone and the slender, instable figures indicate a date before pater's reception piece of 1728, probably around 1725.
provenance: acquired by richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: les plaisirs du bal (the pleasures of the ball)
description: "les plaisirs du bal" (london, dulwich picture gallery) was one of watteau's most successful and most widely copied compositions. p420 is one of several copies produced by pater. one of them was mentioned as being in the artist's studio at the time of his death in 1736. watteau's painting was widely copied by other, unidentified artists as well, but this painting is the only one of these old copies that can confidently be attributed to pater because of its style. the copies follow the actual colours of watteau's work and must have been made - directly or indirectly - after watteau's original and not after the print by gérard scotin of 1731.
provenance: the duc de morny, by 1860; his sale, paris, 02 june 1865, no. 113; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: fête galante by a fountain
description: the painting is a major example of pater' fêtes galantes. the overall composition is based on watteau's "les champs elisées" (p389) that was engraved in 1727. the main group on the right had been developed by pater earlier and reappears in several painting. the background features italianate and flemish elements, a combination that is not uncommon for the ideal pastoral settings of the fêtes galantes. the painting's style is typical for pater's work in the early 1730s. it was sold to lord hertford for 29,000 francs (about £1,160), a record price for pater at the time.
provenance: duc de morny; his sale, paris, 01 june 1865; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: bathing party in a park
description: one of pater's main contributions to the new genre of fêtes galantes were scenes of female bathers. he moved watteau’s invention to a more openly erotic plane replacing careful allusions by hands-on activity. still, the framework of the fête galante stays intact: the group of beautiful young women and men, the ideal southern landscape. the originally carefree atmosphere has considerably changed, for it now aims primarily at male observers and has lost its subdued calm. the earliest examples of female bathers in pater’s work all date from c. 1728/1729, long after watteau’s death. pater pursued the topic until his death. the wallace painting is part of a larger group of similar scenes. an unfinished painting in grenoble might have stayed in pater's studio to be used as a model for several versions.
provenance: acquired by richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: les vivandières de brest (the vivandières of brest)
description: the painting is a good example of the military scenes that pater produced. the theme recalls the rare encampment scenes of antoine watteau (1684–1721) and the very common military pictures of dutch seventeenth-century artists such as philips wouwermans (1619–1668), which were highly prized by eighteenth-century collectors. like watteau, pater did not represent the actual violence of war, but the marches and rests of soldiers off the battle site. pater's reception piece for the paris academy was a similar scene, which indicates the importance of this subject for the painter and his collectors. the title derives from the print made after the composition by le bas (1707–1784) in 1760. it probably refers to the french defense against their british opponents at brest in june 1694. the verses by charles moraine which accompany the print exhort the belles vivandières (or female camp followers), to feed the needy soldiers.
provenance: isaac pereire, by 1864; his sale, paris, 07 march 1872, no. 71; deliére, for sir richard wallace.

title: fête galante with six figures near a fountain
description: the painting is a typical small fête galante by pater. the main group is based on figures in the painter's reception piece for the paris academy (paris, louvre) from 1728 and reappears in several of his works. the seated male figure originally had the same position in the reception piece and was then changed which might indicate that p458 slightly predates the painting in paris.
provenance: acquired by richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: fête galante in a coastal landscape
description: the painting is one of the finest paters in the wallace collection and a beautiful example of a fête galante. the strong colours are typical for pater's later work. pater has painted several variations of the composition, probably all in the 1730s.
provenance: anatole demidoff; his sale, paris, 13 january 1863, no. 10; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: le plaisir de l'été (summer pleasure)
description: in 1743 and 1744, louis surugue published engravings after two horizontal compositions by pater, one under the title "le plaisir de l'été", the other as "le désir de plaire". the latter one depicts a toilet scene in an interior. these two works, probably created by pater as pendants, are today lost. a whole group of paintings with vertical compositions are based on these engravings. they were painted towards the middle of the eighteenth century, after pater's death, in styles different from pater's own. these versions prove that pater's erotic compositions remained highly popular. pater's originals are good examples how, after watteau's death, the fête galante became more narrative and more openly erotic. a vertical version after "le désir de plaire" in the louvre has sometimes been regarded as the pendant to p472 but was painted by a different painter after pater's model.
provenance: f. laneuville; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford, 13 july 1852.

title: robbers in a cornfield
description: the figures appear to be wearing seventeenth-century costume.this low-life, rather disquieting scene is an unexpected purchase for the 4th marquess of hertford, differing markedly from his customary taste.
provenance: commissioned by a viennese collector; anatole demidoff; his sale, paris, 13 january 1863, no. 33; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: the ambuscade
description: a work of inferior quality to pettenkofen's 'robbers in a cornfield' (p338), and probably by a contemporary imitator of the artist. the soldiers are austrian dragoons.
provenance: monsieur [?]; his sale, paris, 5 march 1863, lot 36, bought by richard wallace for 1015 francs, presumably on behalf of richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: jupiter and io
description: the miniature is a nineteenth-century copy after a painting by jean-baptiste-marie pierre painted for voyer d'argenson's chateau asnieres. the subject is taken from ovid, 'metamorposes', i.
provenance: probably acquired by richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: an arab encampment
medium: pencil, watercolour and body on paper
description: presumably painted during one of pils’s visits to algeria in the 1860s. he first visited the country in 1863.
provenance: boussaton sale, paris, 25 april 1868, no 15; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: an idyll: daphnis and chloe
description: the pastoral romance daphnis and chloe by the late greek writer longus (third or fourth century a. d.) tells of the love of two foundlings from noble families. one of the main incidents in their story, illustrated here, depicts the moment when daphnis, alone with the sleeping chloe, notices his former playmate’s beauty and first feels adult passion for her (i, 25). the artist conveys the couple’s youth in their pale slim bodies, and the wonder and longing of the protagonist by the use of restrained but dramatic gesture. a lyrical quality is imparted by the idyllic landscape setting. the picture was previously attributed to giovanni battista bertucci, although he is known only as a painter of religious subjects.
provenance: the vicomte both de tauzia; sir richard wallace, 1872.

title: the abduction of helen
description: p634 is a typical example of the small, detailed paintings on copper showing historical scenes for which johann georg platzer is best known. here, the subject is taken from greek mythology and the picture illustrates the abduction of helen by paris, prince of troy, an episode which resulted in the trojan war. ancient greek sources vary as to the nature of helen’s abduction – it is sometimes described as a forced abduction but also as a calm and consensual event. platzer follows the tradition of western painting, and shows a violent scene of chaos and destruction. a similar composition, showing antony and cleopatra at the battle of actium is in the collection at apsley house, london.the painting was acquired by sir richard wallace in 1872.
provenance: a. beurdeley; sir richard wallace, paris, 05 march 1872.

title: lamentation over a dead hero
medium: brown ink and wash on paper
description: a copy, perhaps from the workshop, of a lost design by pollaiuolo, recalling his interest in the representation of the nude in violent expressive poses, borne out by his known designs such as the battle of the nudes (engraving, c.1470-5). the subject may be identified with the lamentation of the death of pallas, as described in vigil’s aeneid (xi, 29-41). turnus, king of the rutulians, killed pallas, son of evander, king of arcadia, when he was fighting for aeneas in italy. the young man’s corpse was laid out before his tent, where the trojan women loosed their hair in mourning, and ‘all struck their breasts and loud was their lamentation’. the standing figure on the right may be aeneas, while beside him the ageing acoetes bends over the body.
provenance: baron paul von praun, nuremberg; frauenholz, c. 1797; prince miklos esterhazy; the vicomte both de tauzia, 1868; sir richard wallace, 1872.

title: a merry company at table
description: a bordeeltje, or brothel scene, is implied by the discarded rapier, lute and dog in the foreground, symbolizing the disarming power of love and carnal desire. an elderly brothel-keeper watches from a doorway as her girls flirt with the soldiers. the figures seated around the tables make music together, a common euphemism for making love. they also play cards and smoke, both considered vices at the time.
provenance: mary, countess of holderness; her sale, christie's, 06 march 1802, no. 54; stepney. francis charles seymour-conway, 3rd marquess of hertford.

title: herdsmen with their cattle
description: potter here combines animal painting with a genre scene. a couple avoids the glare of the sun by sitting in the patch of the shade afforded by the sheep shelter. their figures are squat and coarse, and their scale is disproportionately large. however, the picture convincingly reflects potter’s fascination with different qualities of light. it was acquired by the 4th marquess of hertford in 1865 for the considerable sum of 41,400 francs (about £1,656) at the paris sale of baron groote lindt.
provenance: baron van brienen van groote lindt, amsterdam, by 1834; groote lindt sale, paris, 08 may 1865, no. 27; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: the milkmaid
description: paulus potter specialised in the depiction of animals in landscape and farmyard scenes. his chief source of inspiration was pieter van laer, who made a series of etchings of domestic animals in 1636. as his career progressed, the animals took on an increasingly prominent place within the composition. potter’s rural subjects reflect the importance of agriculture in the seventeenth-century dutch economy. while describing farm workers and their animals with great care, as in the milkmaid (left), potter emphasises the close connection of his subjects to the earth and gives them an aura of heroic grandeur. a sense of monumentality is created by the low viewpoint, accentuating the size of the animals and the milkmaid. the texture is remarkable: by applying thick white or light yellow paint to the smooth coats of the animals, potter mimics the appearance of individual patches of hair and wool.
provenance: jan danser nijman sale, amsterdam, 16-17 august 1797, no. 207; thomas theodore cremer; his sale, rotterdam, 16-17 april 1816, no. 95; van os, for jurriaans; his sale, amsterdam, 28 august 1817, no. 47; de vries. gerrit schimmelpenninck sale, amsterdam, 12 july 1819, no. 90; van de willigen. mme. hoofman, 1834. richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: cattle in stormy weather
description: potter’s rural subjects reflect the importance of agriculture in the seventeenth-century dutch economy. while describing farm workers and their animals with great care, potter adopts a low viewpoint, creating a broad expanse of sky in which the gathering gloom of a storm is suggested. the picture once belonged to the banker william hope, at whose london sale in 1849 it was bought by the 4th marquess of hertford, who returned the picture to the auctioneer. he changed his mind less than ten years later and re-purchased the painting, paying 20,100 francs (about £804) at the 1858 hope sale in paris.
provenance: the comte de wassenaer d'obdam sale, the hague, 19 august 1750, no. 45; bisschop. mme. bandeville sale, paris, 03 december 1787, no. 26; coclers. claude tolozan sale, paris, 23 february 1801, no. 88. solirène sale, paris, 13 march 1812, no. 88; constantin. charles-ferdinand, duc de berry; the duchesse de berry; christie's, april to june 1834, no. 41; the duchesse du berry sale, paris, 05 april 1837, no. 39; w. williams hope; his sale, christie's, 15 june 1849, no. 111; samuel mawson, for richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford, 1849; richard seymour-conway, 4th marquess of hertford.

title: portrait of a man
description: there is no evidence to support the inscription identifying the sitter as the duc d’alençon (1554-84), younger brother of charles ix and henri iii of france, and no other clue to his identity is given. he wears spanish dress, fashionable with the nobility in the southern netherlands during the turbulent period of spanish rule and protestant revolt. the picture is typical of the 3rd marquess of hertford’s taste for historical portraits.
provenance: [almost certainly 2nd earl of warwick's sales, christie's, 01 june 1801, no. 61, bt. in, and 01 may 1802, no. 122, bt. in]. francis charles seymour-conway, 3rd marquess of hertford.

title: an allegory of true love
